title: 25-year-old nabbed with 400 tablets allegedly for illegal sale
byline: A 25-year-old man was arrested with 400 medicine tablets allegedly intended for illegal sale during a joint Navy-Police operation in Anuradhapura yesterday (29).

title: Police issue strict warning over loudspeaker noise
byline: Police have issued strict guidelines on the use of loudspeakers, amplifiers and sound systems, warning that legal action will be taken against those who create excessive noise and disturb the public.

title: NPP - LG Member in Jaffna Arrested After Allegedly Causing Disturbance While Intoxicated
byline: NPP’s local government member representing the Vadamarachchi South-West Pradeshiya Sabha, Ganesaruban along with several of his friends, was arrested by the Nelliyadi Police for allegedly trespassing into the house of a retired government officer in Nelliyadi, Jaffna, while intoxicated and damaging the house and property.

title: Environment Ministry urges public to ditch single-use plastic bottles
byline: The Ministry of Environment has urged the public to reduce and eventually move away from single-use plastic water bottles, warning that plastic waste can remain in the environment for hundreds of years and cause long-term harm to ecosystems and human health.

title: 200 Japanese tourists depart for Sri Lanka on single flight
byline: A group of 200 Japanese tourists departed for Sri Lanka today on a single SriLankan Airlines flight, marking a significant boost to tourism ties between Sri Lanka and Japan.

title: Nepal-Tibet death toll 750 from Himalayan flood, 3,000 missing
byline: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet from last week’s catastrophic floods hit 750 on Sunday with 3,044 missing, authorities said, while rescuers moved ​to higher ground as rain swelled river levels.

title: Sri Lanka to send disaster relief teams to flood-hit Nepal
byline: Sri Lanka is planning to deploy disaster relief teams to Nepal in the coming days to assist communities affected by severe flooding, Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekara said.

title: CAA dismisses social media posts of price hikes on dairy products
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has dismissed social media posts circulating as “BREAKING NEWS” that claim prices of several dairy products, including milk powder, cultured milk drinks and yoghurt, have been increased.

title: Video dispute ends in death of 17-year-old student
byline: A 17-year-old school student was killed in a sharp weapon attack in  Eheliyagoda early this morning (30), police said.

title: Wheat flour hike pushes up short eats prices
byline: Prices of several flour-based short eats and other eatery items have been increased following a sharp rise in the price of wheat flour, the All-Island Canteen Owners’ Association said.

title: UN, Nepal warn of climate threat after deadly floods
byline: Himalayan glaciers, which provide critical water to nearly 2 billion people, are melting faster as the planet heats, exposing communities to unpredictable, costly disasters.

title: Sri Lanka loses hosting rights for inaugural 2027 Women’s Champions Trophy
byline: Sri Lanka has lost the hosting rights for the inaugural 2027 ICC Women’s Champions Trophy, with the International Cricket Council (ICC) deciding to move the tournament to another country amid the ongoing administrative uncertainty surrounding Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC).

title: Showers expected in several areas after 2 p.m.
byline: Showers or thundershowers may occur at a few places in the Uva Province and in the Ampara, Batticaloa and Hambantota districts after 2 p.m. today, while several spells of showers are expected in the Western and North-western provinces.

title: Underworld figure ‘Welle Saranga’ held in Dubai
byline: Underworld figure Saranga Pradeep, alias “Welle Saranga,” has reportedly been arrested in Dubai based on information provided by Sri Lanka’s Central Crime Investigation Bureau (CCIB) and State Intelligence Service (SIS).

title: Sun overhead Sri Lanka’s latitudes until September 7
byline: The Sun will be directly overhead at various locations in Sri Lanka from August 28 to September 7 due to its apparent southward movement, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Dutch health institute issues ’red alert’ over Trump-shaped ecstasy pills
byline: A Dutch drug addiction and mental health institute has issued a ’’red alert’’ to users about potentially lethal ecstasy pills which resemble US President Donald Trump.

title: Sevanagala factory crisis deepens as production remains halted
byline: The Sevanagala Sugar Factory has been temporarily closed following repeated disruptions to production linked to ongoing employee unrest and trade union action, the Chairman of the Sevanagala Sugar Company said.

title: Police open fire at Narahenpita checkpoint to rescue abducted woman
byline: Police foiled an alleged abduction attempt involving a young woman attending a graduation ceremony at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH) in Colombo today, with officers opening fire at the vehicle after the driver allegedly refused repeated orders to stop.

title: At least 37 dead and hundreds evacuated after strike on Kyiv weapons depot
byline: Thirty-seven people have died and almost 400 evacuated after a Russian drone strike hit a depot storing weapons for Ukraine’s military near a residential area.

title: High waves, sea inundation warning issued for Southern coastal areas
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a warning about high waves and possible seawater inundation in nearshorareas stretching from Beruwala to Matara via Galle.

title: Namal questions government over delays in Sri Lanka’s Digital ID rollout
byline: Claiming that the deadline for the implementation of Sri Lanka’s Digital ID has now passed, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) MP Namal Rajapaksa said that the Government must tell the people clearly when the Digital ID actually would be delivered.

title: Ecuador ex-president Moreno sentenced to five years in jail in bribery case
byline: An Ecuadorian court has found former President Lenin Moreno guilty of bribery in a case tied to the construction of the country’s largest hydroelectric plant, the public prosecutor’s office said on Friday.

title: Foul-smelling paint attack on person who insulted Diyawadana Nilame
byline: Police said that a person who was protesting in front of the Sri Dalada Maligawa while displaying a banner containing insulting remarks about the Diyawadana Nilame of the Sri Dalada Maligawa and the Senior Deputy Inspector General of Police in charge of the Central Province was attacked with paint containing an unpleasant smell.

title: IMF, ILO report triggers government development officers to stage union action?
byline: The recent reports published by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and International Labour Organisation (ILO), which revealed that Sri Lanka is in slot 120 among 130 nations with poor salaries, had prompted the State and Provincial Development Officers Union to stage a protest on Monday, August 31, 2026.

title: Family dispute: Husband murders wife in the wild
byline: Following a family dispute that had escalated, the husband allegedly deceived his wife yesterday (28) and took her to a forest reserve in the Korakahawwa area of Anuradhapura, where he attacked her with a sharp weapon, causing serious injuries and killing her. The Anuradhapura Police said that he subsequently stabbed himself with the same knife, sustaining injuries.

title: Is a referendum on the cards? Opposition MP questions President’s rally plans
byline: Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera has questioned the decision by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to hold a series of rallies from September 5, raising speculation over whether a referendum could be on the cards in relation to the 22nd Amendment.

title: Groundwater levels follow seasonal decline in dry-zone areas
byline: Groundwater levels in several dry-zone areas of Sri Lanka are showing their usual seasonal decline, with the most significant reductions being recorded in Kalpitiya and the Jaffna Peninsula, according to the Water Resources Board.

title: Police to shut down Facebook groups abusing women, children
byline: Sri Lanka Police have taken urgent steps to deactivate Facebook accounts and groups that promote the abuse of women and children by sharing obscene photographs and videos, police said.

title: Bribery Commission officers visit Ravi Karunanayake’s residence
byline: Officers from the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) visited the residence of MP Ravi Karunanayake today, but left after finding that the MP was not in Colombo.

title: Wheat flour prices increased by Rs. 17
byline: The price of wheat flour has been increased by Rs. 17 per kilogram by Prima Ceylon (Pvt) Ltd and Serendib Flour Mills (Pvt) Ltd, with the new prices taking effect from today.

title: Fire breaks out at Embilipitiya Paper Mill
byline: A fire broke out this afternoon (30) at a warehouse used to store waste materials within the premises of the Embilipitiya Paper Mill.

title: Ferry carrying 260 people capsizes off coast of northern Cyprus
byline: A search is underway off the coast of northern Cyprus after a ferry carrying around 260 people capsized, according to local media.

title: Rulers of Muslim nations should recognize ’true enemy,’ says Iran’s supreme leader
byline: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Sunday that rulers of Muslim countries should recognize what he called ’’the true enemy,’’ accusing the US and Israel of being ’’sworn enemies’’ of Islamic unity.

title: Nepal-Tibet death toll 750 from Himalayan flood, 3,000 missing
byline: The death toll in Nepal and Tibet from last week’s catastrophic floods hit 750 on Sunday with 3,044 missing, authorities said, while rescuers moved ​to higher ground as rain swelled river levels.

title: Fuel prices slashed
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (Ceypetco) has announced a reduction in the prices of Petrol 92 and Petrol 95 Octane, effective from midnight today (30).

title: Justice Minister firm on 22nd Amendment
byline: Justice Minister Attorney-at-Law Harshana Nanayakkara has reiterated that the government will move ahead with the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, including provisions to extend the retirement age of judges, while rejecting opposition claims that the reforms are designed to benefit a particular individual.
